text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT FLOUR SALE - Turkish private miller Uncular said on Friday said it had begun selling 25,000 tonnes of wheat flour to Algeria's state company Enial at $305 per tonne.

WHEAT TENDER - Egypt's official Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills said on Friday it was seeking 150,000 tonnes plus or minus 5 percent of U.S. hard red wheat or Australian hard wheat for delivery between April and June. Deadline for the bids is Monday, March 24.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria passed in a tender for the import of 75,000 tonnes of optional-origin milling wheat for April and May because prices offered were too high, European grain exporters said on Friday. Exporters also said they expected Algeria to place another tender for the wheat soon, possibly next week.
- South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd said on Friday it passed on tenders for 24,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat due to high prices. Shipment was set for May 15-June 15 to the western port of Inchon.
WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd said on Friday they passed on tenders for 21,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat due to high offer prices.

- The Cyprus Grain Commission has changed the deadline for the submission of tenders for the supply of a combined cargo of 10,000 tonnes of spring and 8,000 tonnes of durum wheat to March 27, it said in a statement. The commission had earlier issued another announcement saying the deadline expired on March 28. All other terms in the initial tender issued remain the same, it said. Shipment of the cargo is scheduled to take place between April 5 and 20.

WHEAT TENDER - France will hold a tender on March 26 to sell 3,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Iraq via the Rome-based World Food Programme, national grain office ONIC said. The wheat is for shipment April 8-30.
- India's State Trading Corporation (STC) has tendered for 50,000 tonnes of wheat imports for arrival in the post-monsoon season from September onwards, a senior STC official said.
- Iraq received offers in its tender for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat and a reply is expected early next week, some U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for May 15-June 15.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp cancelled a Friday tender for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean due to the government ban on pork export, company buyers said. Taiwan's Council of Agriculture on Thursday banned all exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of the foot and mouth disease in the island's hog population.

CORN TENDERS - Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group passed on a tender for two shipments of U.S. No.2 or Argentine corn, with each shipment ranging between 54,000 and 56,000 tonnes, due to the government's ban on pork export.

SOYBEAN TENDER - The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association passed on a tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of Argentine or Brazilian soybeans, due to the government's ban on prok export.
VEGOIL TENDER - Egypt was seeking up to 45,000 tonnes of assorted vegetable oils for delivery in May 1997. The deadline for all bids was on April 2.
BARLEY TENDER - The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.
RICE TENDER - Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

- Costa Rica has received offers for about 26,500 tonnes optional origin rice which would likely be from the United States and/or Argentina and a reply would be expected early next week, U.S. exporters and trade sources said.
MARKET TALK - Taiwanese corn imports are seen falling sharply after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease that has ravaged the country's pork industry, traders said on Friday.
... Philippine grain importers will probably be glued to the sidelines next week and adopt a wait-and-see attitude due to high prices of U.S. wheat and soybeans, traders said.
